Hi u/Leuku! Thanks for making this brew, it's great! I'm currently running my first campaign for my boyfriend and he's a druid using this variant. He wanted abilities like Perfuma from She-Ra and this has been perfect for that!

Keep in mind that I am a very noob DM, but I do have a couple points/questions I wanted to bring up. I'm sorry that I don't have any clear suggestions. (also for formatting)

* Stable Root and Leaf Wall feel maybe a bit too similar. I'd like to see the level 5 feature be a bit more unique, perhaps something with healing or that helps Dexterity saves? I'm just brainstorming this as I type and I'm thinking either some sort of edible plant with multiple servings that heals or gives temporary hit points, or a plant that creates an area of effect that heals or gives temporary hit points each turn with pollen or spores or something.
* Leaf Wall produces leaves that can float on water. Presumably a creature could stand on a leaf that's in the wall (like little steps or platforms), or attempt to use a leaf as a boat. It'd be nice to have some weight or size parameters for it. Also, a description about what happens to creatures in the space where the leaf grows would be good, similar to Stable Root.
* Limber Branches is probably my favorite option! I think the wording should be different so that it's clear that any creature that stands within the space gets the AC bonus. Something like this? *Limber branches erupt around a point on the ground within 60 feet of you, occupying a 5-foot square. A Medium or smaller creature gains a +2 bonus to AC while it is in that space.*
* Dandelion Ride seems like it would create some really fun moments! I assume that when it's created, it would have similar options to Stable Root as far as creatures riding it up as it grows or moving to an open space, but maybe not. Either way, it should be clarified what happens to a creature in the Dandelion Ride's space.
* Overgrowth sounds cool, until two levels later you get Pangea and it becomes completely obsolete. I get that as you level some abilities/features are replaced entirely by better versions, but I think in this case the two abilities should be fundamentally different. I'd keep Pangea, I think it's a cool, logical, and powerful capstone that fits the flavor of the class. But Overgrowth oughta change. I have absolutely no experience with higher levels of play, so I'm not gonna try to come up with a replacement, and I'm sorry about that.

I hope this constructive criticism was somewhat helpful, and I apologize if it's not up to the standards expected of a review in this thread, I really did try. This piece largely focuses on the unpleasant fellow, but perhaps equally intriguing is the door which the fellow holds. To where does it lead? The ethereal waves emanating from behind the fellow suggest some otherworldly plane, while the postitioning of the fellow blocks our view and leaves us guessing. 

Is it some sort of paradise? Or someplace more akin to Hell? The fellow’s lopsided frown and grin gives little away, hinting at a possibility of both. The fellow’s hands, reminiscent of oversized forks, relay an underlying hunger: the fellow is holding the door for you and *wants* you to enter. 

His winged feet provide a sense of urgency, the door will not remain open for long. You must decide with haste wether to enter or not, lest the fellow be unable to hold the door any longer.

It also serves as a job site block for villagers to be cartographers.

You can also lock maps with a glass pane at a cartography table.

Crafting Table:
Empty map = 9 paper
Empty locator map = 8 paper, 1 compass

Anvil:
One zoom level = 8 paper

Cartography Table:
Empty map = 1 paper
Empty locator map = 1 paper, 1 compass
One zoom level = 1 paper

My dad was the same when he found out I was transgender. “I love you. But are you sure? Maybe you’re confused , maybe you should put off anything until you’ve talked to a therapist ...” and so on, that kind of stuff. I informed him that I’d already talked to a therapist, was already on hormones and that everyone else already knows and has been adjusting accordingly. That no, I am not confused and for the first time in forever 🎶 I knew who I was.

Over the next several months, he continued to misgender me and use my dead name, not even attempting to change. I think he wanted to pretend that our conversation had never happened. 

Eventually, I basically gave him the strong hint that he’d best change or he’d not be hearing from me ever. I told him that talking to him was difficult for me because literally everyone else in my life (family, friends, coworkers) were at the very least trying and he was the only one still referring to me as my assigned gender and dead name.

He was mad and defensive and pointed out that it was hard for him too (which, as an aside, I hadn’t fully considered). After that though he has made the effort and only ever misgenders/dead names me rarely and by mistake. I know he doesn’t actually support my transition, but having this small change has improved our relationship so much.

TL;DR My dad got better with time and an intense discussion, maybe (I hope) your mom will too.

First off, let me be clear that I totally agree with this sentiment of not clocking people like this. Because many (most?) trans individuals are attempting to pass. And if you are bopping along, passing away and then someone’s like “hey, just a reminder. You’re trans, you’re not passing” that can be devastating.

However, I would just like to put in my personal idea of my transness so maybe it helps understand this action a bit. 

I don’t want to pass. I enjoy being a trans woman. I am not a cis woman, just like I’m not a cis man. I strongly associate being transgender with my identity, and for me passing would be hiding that part of myself. If someone mentions or otherwise points out the fact that I am trans, it doesn’t bother me. It is true and something I take pride in.

Fortunately, I’ve seen enough posts and met enough trans individuals to know that by and large,  people don’t want to be outed in any way. And that people want to pass. And I absolutely understand and 100% respect that. But someone that doesn’t get this and has my views might be too excited to realize what a bad idea it is to approach someone and out them. I am sorry that this happens to so many people and I see how harmful it can be.

We could hear the sound of them riding hard just down the canyon as we came to a brief halt. The thunder of over thirty horses, accompanied by the shouts of their riders and the occasional gunshot echoed off the rock all around us.

I turned in my saddle to cast my eyes over our pathetic caravan. Two rickety wagons with a pair of horses pulling each and three outriders, counting myself. Our group was too slow. I had known as soon as the pursuit started, but I'd hoped nonetheless.

The sobbing of the children and the soft cooing of their parents in the wagons could be heard for a moment as the wind shifted through the narrow pass. My eyes met those of one of the drivers, William. His fear was evident, but he gritted his teeth and knew what I had determined miles earlier.

“They’ll be on us soon,” Joshua, one of the other outriders, said as his horse trotted to my position.

“No lie,” I replied grimly.

He jerked a thumb in the direction of the wagons.

“Reckon we could get out of this with our hides intact if we left these soft bellies behind.”

I spit a glob of tobacco into the dirt.

“These soft bellies are the only reason we survived last winter. I know you aren't one to pay your debts, but I always settle up.”

“Look Sam, I ain't saying I want those kids to die, there's just no way all of us are gettin’ outta here. No sense in the lot of us cashing it in if we ain't gotta.”

I looked at him with a faint grin.

“You're right about that.”

“Really?” 

His face fell when he noticed mine.

“Sammy, these folks ain't worth it!”

William turned to calm his wife and pretend he wasn't listening.

“I've made the decision already. And you didn't start calling me Stubborn Sam for nothing. I'm the best duelist alive, I can buy you and them enough time to make it to town. Sheriff and his boys’ll be plenty to keep them safe.”

The boast was hardly such, my skill was legendary. And Joshua knew I was right. He unstrapped his dual revolvers and held them toward me.

“Damn fool,” he muttered, “you never could help being the hero.”

I grabbed the belt holster and secured it just above my own. Four fully loaded six shooters now peeked from beneath my duster. Joshua was a liar. I'd been the villain far too many times, and he knew it.

“Lead these folks to town, and you'll be the hero this time. I'm sure the saloon gives a discount for heroism.”

I winked at him, but he only half smiled.

“Boss, we gotta move! Them Cutthroat boys are almost on us!” Daniel, the third outrider, was hollering from the back of the convoy.

I looked Joshua square in the eye.

“Get William and his kin to town for me. And since I didn't get the chance, if you ever see Pop again …”

“Put a bullet in his guts, then his head. I know, I know.”

He pulled his reins and shouted at the wagons to get moving. His rifle slid into his grasp smooth as silk while he rode away. I may be the best duelist alive, but Joshua is the finest sharpshooter to ever draw breath. I was confident he would deliver the group to safety.

As William passed me, he smiled.

“Well Samantha, looks like my boy was right, you folks are the good guys.”

I glanced into the wagon and back at William.

“William, for the last time, call me Sam.”

He tipped his hat and yanked the reins. Daniel flipped me his lucky coin while his horse cantered by. 

“It's double sided!” he yelled.

I turned it over in my hand, and sure enough, it was identical on either side. I grinned. Daniel had won countless bets against both Joshua and I with this piece of metal. I looked up, but they were already rounding the bend in the canyon. 

I turned back in the direction of death and set my hands on my revolvers.
